frame: Sentence-final restrictive participial phrase after 'examined the specimens', containing its own where-clause; the last sentence names a second examined set (meteorites from the interior), with no 'by contrast' marker
structure: Left: a complete clause ending 'examined the specimens'. Right: 'gathered where the blue ice meets a dark moraine of wind-scoured gravel', a participial phrase that ends the sentence and contains a finite verb only inside its where-clause. Restrictiveness is settled by the last sentence, which shows a second set the team also examined.
decider_quote: Meteorites the team recovered from the field's frozen interior showed almost no rust

distractor_pulls.specimens, gathered: A participial phrase after a complete clause is very often set off with a comma, and 'the specimens' reads as the team's known set.
distractor_pulls.specimens—gathered: A dash reads as the natural mark for a trailing descriptive add-on about where the specimens came from.
distractor_pulls.specimens. Gathered: 'Gathered where the blue ice meets a dark moraine' contains a subject and verb ('the blue ice meets'), so the new sentence looks complete unless the reader sees that 'meets' belongs to the where-clause.

distractor_kills.specimens, gathered: Nonrestrictive punctuation says every specimen examined came from the moraine edge; the last sentence ('Meteorites the team recovered from the field's frozen interior showed almost no rust') shows the team examined a second set, so the phrase is restrictive and takes no comma.
distractor_kills.specimens—gathered: Same rule: a dash also marks the phrase as nonessential.
distractor_kills.specimens. Gathered: The words after the period have no main clause: 'meets' is the verb of the subordinate where-clause, so the result is a fragment.

heuristics_that_give_key: 'by contrast' no longer flags the second set; the reader must see that the meteorites in the last sentence were also examined
hostile_reader.changed: REVISION: removed 'by contrast' (r0: it handed over the restrictive reading); the phrase after the blank now contains a where-clause with a finite verb so the period option is not a visible fragment; first sentence 'but' -> 'yet'

frame: 'were taken' against 'are taken'; plural head 'readings' preceded by singular possessive 'harbor's' and followed by 'from the old stone pier' (adjacent); past inferred from a participial phrase naming a structure that no longer exists (no time word)
decider_quote: bolted to a long-demolished timber landing stage
deletion_test: Delete the participial phrase and 'the harbor's handwritten readings from the old stone pier are taken from a painted wooden staff' is as correct as 'were taken'; the coordinated clause ('the ledgers' margins hold') is present and does not fix the time.

distractor_pulls.are taken: Every other verb in the passage is present ('come', 'hold'), and 'According to the port's archivist' frames a present report, so the present passive reads as a description of how the pier's readings are made.
distractor_pulls.is taken: The subject opens with singular 'harbor's' and the noun before the blank is singular 'pier'; the present matches the surrounding verbs.
distractor_pulls.was taken: A reader who infers the past from the demolished landing stage but takes 'harbor's ... pier' as the number lands here.

distractor_kills.are taken: Tense: the staff was 'bolted to a long-demolished timber landing stage', a structure that no longer exists, so the readings belong to a finished past; a present verb is an error.
distractor_kills.is taken: Agreement: the head is plural 'readings'; also wrong in tense.
distractor_kills.was taken: Agreement: 'readings' is plural; 'harbor's' is a possessive determiner and 'pier' is inside the from-phrase.

frame: Passive present perfect required by the present-tense matrix 'The plant's new installation marks the first time that ...'; singular head 'bank' + 'above the lithography bays' adjacent to the blank. The present clause stating the current situation comes BEFORE the blank

deletion_test: Replace the matrix with a plain statement ('The filter bank above the lithography bays ______ by a design containing no glass fiber') and 'was superseded' is as correct as 'has been superseded'; the requirement comes only from the present 'marks the first time that'.

distractor_pulls.have been superseded: 'bays' sits right before the blank and the perfect is right, so a reader who checks only the tense picks it.
distractor_pulls.was superseded: Replacing a filter bank is a single finished event, and the simple past is the default way to report one; most readers do not know the 'first time' rule.
distractor_pulls.were superseded: Both lures: the plural 'bays' and the finished-event simple past.

distractor_kills.was superseded: Tense: after a present-tense 'marks the first time that', the counted event must be in the present perfect; the simple past is an error in this construction.
distractor_kills.were superseded: Agreement and tense, both as above.

distractor_pulls.are always: The plural 'charts' opens the sentence, and the be-reading is grammatical up to 'peak'.
distractor_pulls.have always: A reader who spots 'subsided' but takes the plural 'charts' as the subject.

structure: Left: 'damage was heaviest in the fishing villages closest to the earthquake's epicenter', a complete clause. Right: 'located beneath a shallow bay south of the harbor town', a participial phrase describing the epicenter, ending the sentence.

distractor_pulls.epicenter located: 'located beneath ...' after a noun is very often restrictive ('the town located on the bay'), and no comma is the cleanest option.
distractor_pulls.epicenter. Located: The clause before the blank is complete, and a reader may start a new sentence at the long participial phrase.
distractor_pulls.epicenter: located: The location of the epicenter seems to explain why the villages nearest it were hit, so a colon looks like it introduces an explanation.

distractor_kills.epicenter located: A restrictive phrase picks one member out of a set; 'the earthquake's epicenter' has only one possible referent, so the phrase is nonrestrictive and must be set off with a comma.
distractor_kills.epicenter. Located: The participial phrase has no subject or main verb: a fragment.
distractor_kills.epicenter: located: A colon must introduce something that explains or restates the whole clause; a participial phrase modifying the noun 'epicenter' does not.

distractor_pulls.is swung by it: The sentence just before the blank is about a single motor ('No motor working alone ... a reflector'), so 'it' looks like it refers to the motor, the obvious kind of thing that swings a dish.
distractor_pulls.are swung by it: The plural 'bursts' sits just before the subject and 'arcs' just after; the singular pronoun again points at 'motor'.
distractor_pulls.are swung by them: A reader who finds the plural motors may let the plural spread to the verb, helped by 'bursts' and 'arcs' around the blank.

distractor_kills.is swung by it: Pronoun-antecedent agreement: the only possible antecedent is plural 'motors' (first sentence). 'No motor' is a negative quantifier and cannot be picked up by a pronoun in a later sentence, and 'dish', the subject of the same clause, would need 'itself'.
distractor_kills.are swung by it: Agreement: the subject 'dish' is singular; pronoun also wrong.
distractor_kills.are swung by them: Subject-verb agreement: 'dish' is singular; 'bursts' is inside the opening phrase.

distractor_pulls.were being cranked: 'prisms' sits right before the blank and 'keepers' right after; a reader who infers the past but matches the nearest plural lands here.

frame: Active present perfect 'have carved' against past progressive 'were carving'; plural head 'surges' after singular possessive 'reservoir's', + 'from the end of the spillway' adjacent; inside 'Surveys by engineers show that'; the first sentence is past-tense narration to strengthen 'were carving'

distractor_pulls.has carved: The subject opens with singular 'reservoir's' and the noun before the blank is singular 'spillway'; the perfect is right, so a reader who checks only aspect picks it.
distractor_pulls.was carving: The first sentence narrates in the past ('designed'), the progressive suits slow erosion, and the singular matches 'reservoir's ... spillway'.
distractor_pulls.were carving: Continues the past narration of the first sentence and describes gradual erosion vividly; it agrees with 'surges'.

distractor_kills.were carving: Aspect: 'which is why the chute's foundation sits beneath water ...' reports a present result of the carving; a past progressive needs a past reference time, which the sentence never gives, and cannot be the cause of a present state.

distractor_pulls.has also: Both pulls: the singular 'anchorage' and the perfect continuation.

distractor_kills.have also: Auxiliary: 'brittle' is an adjective; 'have' cannot link a subject to an adjective without 'been'.

Whether the name is restrictive depends on how many ships the institute used, stated two sentences back.

distractor_pulls.ship Kittiwake: Ship names after a common noun are often written with no punctuation ('the trawler Kittiwake Star'), and the passage already sets off the description that follows with a comma.
distractor_pulls.ship. Kittiwake: 'Kittiwake Star, a trawler the cooperative refitted for coring' contains a subject-verb pair ('the cooperative refitted'), so it can pass for a sentence on a quick read.
distractor_pulls.ship Kittiwake,: A reader unsure where the name ends may take 'Kittiwake' as the name and 'Star' as the start of the description.

distractor_kills.ship Kittiwake: A restrictive name would distinguish this ship from the institute's other ships; the first sentence ('were raised by the same ship') says there was only one, so the name is nonrestrictive and must be set off.
distractor_kills.ship. Kittiwake: No main verb: 'refitted' is the verb of the reduced relative clause modifying 'trawler', so 'Kittiwake Star, a trawler ...' is a fragment.
distractor_kills.ship Kittiwake,: A comma cannot separate the words of a proper name ('Kittiwake Star'); it is wrong by rule, and the name is also left restrictive.
